title: Add tests and a consumer release note for the User consent fields
description: Add tests/test_user_consent.py to onfinance-db-model-master. Using mongomock (or mongoengine connect with mongomock://), the tests check four things: (a) a User without consent fields saves and reloads; (b) a User with consent_id, register purpose ids, notice_version and consent_given_at round-trips unchanged; (c) an unknown purpose or notice id fails validation; (d) setting consent_withdrawn_at keeps the earlier consent fields for audit. Add a CHANGELOG.md entry for 1.1.0 that tells consuming internal services to set consent_id, consent_purposes, notice_version and consent_given_at at onboarding, and warns that downgrading to 1.0.0 fails on documents that hold the new fields (mongoengine strict mode). Merge only after one approval, per sdlc/policy.json approvalsRequired.
acceptanceCriteria: python -m pytest tests/test_user_consent.py exits 0 with the four cases (a) to (d) passing
CHANGELOG.md has a 1.1.0 entry naming the five new fields, the onboarding instruction for consumers and the downgrade warning.
The pull request that merges tasks 2 and 3 has one approving review recorded before merge.

verificationMethod.description: A reviewer other than the author checks out the merged commit, runs python -m pytest tests/test_user_consent.py and reads CHANGELOG.md. Expected result: four passing tests covering legacy load, round-trip, invalid-id rejection and withdrawal retention, plus a 1.1.0 changelog entry with the consumer onboarding instruction and the downgrade warning.

rootCause.description: The library had no tests or release notes covering personal-data fields. Consumers would not learn that consent references must be populated, and a regression that drops them would go unnoticed.
